title: "Builders"
subtitle: "Constructing arrays incrementally in Mojo"

Arrays in Marrow are **immutable** — once built, their buffers never change.
Builders are the mutable staging area where you accumulate values before
freezing them into an array with `finish()`. This is the Mojo-level API; from
Python you use `ma.array()` directly.

::: {.callout-note}
The code on this page is Mojo, not Python. It shows the native API that backs
the Python bindings.
:::

## Primitive builders

A `PrimitiveBuilder[T]` collects fixed-size scalars. Use the typed aliases
(`Int64Builder`, `Float64Builder`, …) when the type is known:

```mojo
from marrow.builders import Int64Builder
from marrow.arrays import Int64Array

var b = Int64Builder(capacity=4)
b.append(10)
b.append(20)
b.append_null()          # marks a null position
b.append(40)

var arr: Int64Array = b.finish()
print(arr)               # Int64Array([10, 20, NULL, 40])
```

`capacity` is a hint that pre-allocates the backing buffer; it is optional but
avoids reallocation when you know the size up front.

## String builders

`StringBuilder` accumulates variable-length UTF-8 strings, tracking offsets for
you:

```mojo
from marrow.builders import StringBuilder
from marrow.arrays import StringArray

var sb = StringBuilder()
sb.append("hello")
sb.append_null()
sb.append("world")

var strs: StringArray = sb.finish()
print(strs)              # StringArray([hello, NULL, world])
```

## Nested builders

Nested builders compose: a `ListBuilder` wraps a child builder for its elements.
Append child values, then commit each list element with `append(True)` (or
`append_null()` for a null list):

```mojo
from marrow.builders import ListBuilder, Int32Builder
from marrow.arrays import ListArray

var child = Int32Builder()
child.append(1)
child.append(2)

var lb = ListBuilder(child^)   # move the child builder in
lb.append(True)                # commit [1, 2] as the first list

lb.values().append(3)          # push a child value for the next list
lb.append(True)                # commit [3] as the second list

lb.append_null()               # a null list in the third position

var lists: ListArray = lb.finish()
```

`StructBuilder` and `FixedSizeListBuilder` follow the same shape — build the
children, then commit rows.

## Type-erased builders

`AnyBuilder` is the runtime-typed builder. Construct one from a `DataType` when
the type is only known at run time; typed builders convert to it implicitly:

```mojo
from marrow.builders import AnyBuilder, Int64Builder
from marrow.dtypes import int64

# from a runtime DataType
var dyn = AnyBuilder(int64())

# a typed builder converts implicitly — no explicit AnyBuilder(...) wrapper
var typed = Int64Builder()
var erased: AnyBuilder = typed
```

`finish()` on an `AnyBuilder` returns an `AnyArray`, the type-erased array
container.

## Why builders?

Building into an immutable array up front means the resulting array can be
shared with O(1) copies (a ref-count bump), passed to compute kernels without
defensive copying, and handed across the Arrow C Data Interface without
touching the data. The mutable/immutable split keeps ownership explicit and the
read path allocation-free.
